paper_title: Constraints on bosonic dark matter from ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance
suggested_experiment_name: CASPEr-ZULF (Cosmic Axion Spin-Precession-Experiment using an Ultralow-field Laser-Free setup)
coupling_convention: g_an (dimensionless axion-neutron coupling), as plotted on y-axis in GeV^-1 units converted to dimensionless form
notes: Paper constrains multiple coupling types: (1) ALP wind-nucleon linear coupling (g_aN, primary result in Fig. 3), (2) ALP quadratic coupling (g_quad, Fig. 4), and (3) dark-photon couplings (g_dEDM and g_dMDM, Fig. 5). The pre-analysis hint suggested AxionElectron, but the paper's main results focus on nuclear-spin couplings, not electron couplings. The primary exclusion (Fig. 3, red shaded region labeled 'CASPEr-ZULF') constrains the ALP wind-nucleon linear coupling g_aN over the mass range 1.8×10^-16 to 7.8×10^-14 eV at 90% CL. The y-axis of Fig. 3 shows g_aN in GeV^-1, spanning roughly 10^-4 to 10^-10. The exact numerical values are difficult to read from the figure; the data_points represent a conservative horizontal bound at the approximate upper limit (~10^-4 GeV^-1) spanning the full mass range. The paper assumes a local dark-matter density ρ_DM ≈ 0.4 GeV/cm³ (standard galactic halo assumption). Confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the coupling type is clear from the paper's focus on nuclear spins and the explicit mention of g_aN, but (2) the exact numerical limits are difficult to extract precisely from the figures without access to supplementary tables, and (3) the paper actually constrains three different coupling types simultaneously, requiring a choice of which to report as primary.
